source: hand-seeded from task D01FEE1F (spec abandoned and deleted; its drafts are in the session record of task 2D916668), replaced by task 2D916668 SPEC.md (Summary, the lookups criteria, Hints: copying servers between Claude config dirs is out of scope)
summary: The owner already has their MCP servers installed (docs servers and a code-search plugin) and names them in `~/.agent/config.json` `mcp` (a copy is in the working directory as `.agent/config.json`). Install renders those servers into the read-only agents' `tools:` lists, which works for sessions on `~/.claude`. A session on a second Claude config dir, such as `~/.claude-work`, has no MCP servers, so its crew agents fall back to text search. Install now mirrors the configured servers: it copies each definition from `~/.claude.json` into every other recorded config dir's `.claude.json`, at the same scope, records each copy in the install manifest, and never overwrites a server the user defined there.
defect: The wrong fix for the need. Copying server definitions into Claude Code's own state file (`<dir>/.claude.json`) duplicates the owner's configuration (headers, env, per-dir OAuth sign-in), drifts from the source, needs manifest bookkeeping and uninstall, and still misses plugin-provided servers, which live under `<dir>/plugins/`, not in `.claude.json`. The servers are already installed and the agents already have them in their tool lists; what was missing is instructions telling every working agent when and how to use them. History abandoned the mirroring spec: no copying; one shared lookups reference that each crew agent points to, plus doctor fixes (detect plugin servers, check only projects with crew work, report without telling the owner to configure Claude).

after.install.sh:
# Link agents, skills and rules into every Claude config dir, and render the read-only agents' tools.
while IFS= read -r dir; do
  link_config_dir "$dir"
done < <(python3 "$SCRIPT_DIR/.claude/install_blocks.py" config-dirs)
render_readonly_agents
# Sessions on a second config dir (such as ~/.claude-work) get the same MCP servers as ~/.claude.
run python3 "$SCRIPT_DIR/.claude/install_blocks.py" mirror-mcp
